definition: Negligible means so small in amount or degree as to be not worth considering.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word negligible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know negligible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The engineers reported that the thicker insulation raised the car's total weight by a negligible amount, less than the weight of a water bottle.
A minor cost is small but still worth noting, while a negligible cost is so small it is not worth considering at all.
A negligible amount is real but too tiny to matter, whereas a nonexistent amount is not there at all.

Slight means small in degree: a slight delay, a slight improvement. A slight thing can still deserve a mention. Negligible goes further: the amount is so small it can be safely ignored altogether. A slight cost still gets a line in the budget; a negligible one does not.

Minute means extremely small in size or amount, like a minute crack in a lens, yet minute things can still matter enormously. Negligible adds a verdict: the amount is too small to have any effect worth considering. Plenty of minute amounts are anything but negligible.

Insignificant means too small to have any real effect or leave any mark, and it can dismiss anything: a detail, an event, a person. Negligible is the more technical cousin, aimed at amounts and degrees. A negligible risk or increase is one you can drop from the calculation.

The negligent groundskeeper let the fountain run dry for a month, showing the same Latin root of 'disregarding' that hides inside negligible.
Negligible means so small in amount or degree as to be not worth considering.
The nutritionist reassured the worried caller that the trace of sodium in the sparkling water was negligible.
At two milligrams per bottle, the amount was far too small to have any effect on even the strictest diet.
Two milligrams is a real amount, but it is so small in quantity that it can be safely ignored, which is exactly what negligible means.

Negligible describes a quantity or degree so small it can be safely ignored, as in 'a negligible risk,' 'a negligible increase in cost,' or 'a negligible amount of rainfall.' Trivial, also taught in this unit, describes something unimportant in a different way: it is about the significance of a matter or issue rather than the size of an amount.
Do not confuse negligible with negligent, which describes a person who carelessly fails to take proper care of something.

When Milbrook's drought committee met to ration water, one member proposed a crackdown on the town's decorative fountains.
The utility's analyst, Rosa Kim, ran the numbers before the next meeting and put a single slide on the screen.
Every fountain in town together drew two-hundredths of one percent of daily use — a negligible amount, she said, next to lawns, which drew a third.
Shutting off every fountain would buy the reservoir less than one extra hour per summer.
A modest cut to watering schedules would buy it three weeks.
The committee dropped the fountain plan from the agenda that night and never took it up again.
